hook: How far one break-in can reach before it hits a wall.
definition: How much one failure or break-in can reach. Systems are built so one stolen key cannot open everything.
example: Railway encrypts each environment's variables with its own key. After its breach, it said at most 1.85% of workspaces could have had variables decrypted.
the_catch: It is not a count of victims. Railway's 1.85% was an upper bound, because its logs identify environments, not individual variables.
caption: Blast radius is how much one failure or break-in can reach. Railway's design meant one compromised key could not expose the whole platform, and it says at most 1.85% of workspaces had variables decrypted. Would you rather one big lock or many small ones?
alt_text: A glossary carousel defining blast radius: how much one failure or break-in can reach, an example from an earlier gummietech post about Railway's breach, and the common mistake of reading it as a count of victims.
attribution: Railway, “Incident Report: October 21st Security Attack”, 10 Nov 2026

es.hook: Hasta dónde puede llegar una intrusión antes de encontrarse con un límite
es.definition: El alcance de una falla o una intrusión. Los sistemas se construyen de modo que una clave robada no pueda abrir todo.
es.example: Railway cifra las variables de cada entorno con su propia clave. Tras la brecha, dijo que, como máximo, el 1,85 % de los entornos de trabajo podrían haber tenido sus variables descifradas.
es.the_catch: No se trata de un recuento de víctimas. El 1,85 % de Railway era un límite superior, ya que sus registros identifican entornos, no variables individuales.
